verdict: The copy is disciplined, specific and in the creator's own register: every heading is two lines at 1440 and 390, no banned words, pricing is exact, the preview is honest, and lines like "Good ideas die in bad first lines" and "Their yes before anything posts" are best-in-class. It falls just short of 9.5 because the Try box, the one place a visitor tests the headline promise on their own line, can leave obvious fluff standing under a "Why it hits" label with no caveat, plus a few small phrasing snags.
to_95: Make the Try box result match "The fluff goes" on crypto-idiom lines: when a sharpened result still contains flagged hedges or doubled intensifiers ("to be honest", "very very", "thrilled"), either cut them or show the existing note "Quick on-device check. In the app, Claude edits it and goes further. Still free." on that result (it currently shows only on Nothing-to-cut results) and swap the label from "Why it hits" to "What changed".
Rewrite the pricing footnote sentence "Ten reply drafts you ask for use one rewrite." so it parses on first read.
Give the Results heading a concrete, creator-voiced line instead of the generic "Know what landed and what to write next."

issues.where: #sharpen Try box, any width. Paste: "just a quick reminder that not financial advice but $SOL looks very very strong here to be honest" (also "Really excited to finally share that after months of hard work our team is thrilled to launch v2").
issues.problem: Under the heading "Your facts stay. The fluff goes." the result is "not financial advice but $SOL looks very very strong here to be honest" with "Cut 1 bit of fluff", a "Why it hits" explanation and the CTA "Keep it. Start free". "very very" and "to be honest" are visibly still there (the same engine cuts "honestly" in the hero example), and the on-device caveat is not shown on this result. For the crypto-first audience, trailing hedges are the most likely thing they paste, so the visitor's own test contradicts the headline and "Why it hits" overclaims. Second line returns "Our team is thrilled to launch v2", which keeps the exact launch-speak the Studio never-say list mocks.
issues.fix: Preferably cut trailing "to be honest"/"tbh", doubled intensifiers ("very very") and "is thrilled to" in the on-device rules. Regardless, when a sharp result still has flagged words (or always on sharp results), show the existing line "Quick on-device check. In the app, Claude edits it and goes further. Still free." under the card, and label the explanation "What changed" instead of "Why it hits" for results from the visitor's own line.

issues.problem: "Ten reply drafts you ask for use one rewrite." stacks "ask for use" and needs a second read; it is the one sentence on the page that trips.
issues.fix: Change to: "One rewrite gives you three takes on a line, or ten reply drafts when you ask for them. Reply-ping drafts are free."

issues.where: #results h2 "Know what landed and what to write next."
issues.problem: The only heading that reads like a generic analytics tool; every other heading has a concrete image or a time ("Say it at 11 PM. Post it at 8:40 AM.").
issues.fix: Use the card's own content, e.g. "What landed. / What to write next." or "More replies than usual? / Here's what to write next." (two lines at 1440 and 390).

issues.where: #sharpen, engine output for "In this issue I want to talk about why your open rate is lying to you and what to do about it"
issues.problem: Result ends with an added colon ("...what to do about it:") that the writer did not type, while the page says only fluff goes and offers no word about added punctuation; the Who-it's-for newsletter example shows a cleaner form of the same line.
issues.fix: Do not append a colon unless the draft had one, or add it to the status chip ("Cut 1 bit of fluff · Added a colon").

issues.where: Hero mock, Try box, final CTA status chips
issues.problem: "Cut 2 bits of fluff" / "Cut 1 bit of fluff" appears in every demo; by the third sighting the cute phrasing reads as a tic, and "1 bit of fluff" is slightly awkward.
issues.fix: Keep "bits of fluff" in the hero only; elsewhere use "Cut 2 phrases" / "Cut 1 phrase" (or name it: "Cut ‘so basically’").
